subject: Discovery: observability + evals — reference prompts, tracing hooks, SLO checklist
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
To: Chris Dalton <chris@finlogic.co>, Amit Shah <amit.shah@finlogic.co>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 22 May 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery: observability + evals — reference prompts, tracing hooks, SLO checklist

Thanks for a focused session today — appreciate the time. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a single source of truth.

Key pain points we heard
- Lack of visibility into model-level regressions: hard to tell whether model changes or prompt drift cause quality drops.
- Cost surprises at token scale: poor per-route breakdowns make it hard to budget.
- No reliable production tracing hooks: latency and tail behavior are opaque across microservices and LLM runtime.

Current stack you shared
- Inference: in-house endpoints on GCP (NVIDIA A100s) with a thin orchestration layer
- Observability: Datadog for infra metrics; limited traces; custom logging for prompts in S3
- Evals: ad-hoc pytest-based checks and manual spot-checks from the product team

Success criteria you highlighted
- Regression detection within 24 hours for high-risk routes (customer-facing summaries)
- Per-route cost per 1k tokens estimate with 10% margin of error
- Tracing that ties user request -> model call -> token-level latency and KV-cache miss rates

Requested deliverables (from us)
1) Example dashboard set (high-level + drilldowns): token cost, per-route latency P50/P95, regression alert summary, eval pass rates
2) Tracing hooks spec (span names, attributes to capture, guardrails for PII)
3) Reference prompt sets (initial seed of 50 prompts per route) and evaluation rubric (precision/recall style + human review thresholds)
4) Rollout/rollback guardrails: automatic fallback to smaller model + canary metrics thresholds

Attachments: observability_requirements.xlsx (requirements template), reference_prompt_set_v1.csv (seed prompts)

Proposed next steps
- I will share the Drive doc with the dashboard mockups and tracing spec by Tue, May 25.
- Schedule a technical dive with your infra + security and our runtime engineers next week (suggest Wed/Thu afternoon PT).
- Marissa (CS) will draft a 6-week POC scope with measurable metrics we can commit to.

Questions for you before the technical dive
- Which internal team owns the token billing attribution today? (product or finance)
- Any strict data residency/KMS constraints we should flag ahead of time?
- Are there existing SLOs for model output quality we should align to?

Thanks — I’ll follow up with the Drive link and calendar invites.

—
Soojin Lee
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
soojin@redwood.com | (415) 555-0143
Redwood Inference

---

From: Chris Dalton <chris@finlogic.co>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
Cc: Amit Shah <amit.shah@finlogic.co>
Date: Sat, 22 May 2027 17:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery: observability + evals — reference prompts, tracing hooks, SLO checklist

Thanks Soojin — great write-up and matches our notes. A few clarifications:

1) Registry/ownership: finance currently pulls billing but product owns route-level attribution (we have a tagging convention in our request headers). We'll share the header spec before the dive.
2) Security: we need KMS-backed keys for any persisted KV or prompt logs. SOC2 stuff is non-negotiable; please flag what info you need for our security review.
3) Timeline: procurement is fairly fast for POC (2–3 weeks) but full production rollout will be end-of-Q3 at earliest.

Two asks from our side before the tech deep dive:
- Can you provide a sample dashboard mock that shows how you surface a regression alert and the drilldown to the failing prompt set?
- Ballpark cost delta for adding per-request tracing (we expect some overhead) — even a percent range is helpful for our infra team.

I attached a quick CSV of the three routes we want covered in the POC and a small sample of production prompts so you can validate matching logic.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — looking forward to the next call.

—
Chris Dalton
Head of Product, FinLogic
chris@finlogic.co

[Attachment: finlogic_poc_routes.csv (csv)]

From: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
To: Chris Dalton <chris@finlogic.co>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Amit Shah <amit.shah@finlogic.co>
Date: Sun, 23 May 2027 08:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery: observability + evals — reference prompts, tracing hooks, SLO checklist

Appreciate the fast reply, Chris — answers inline and owners assigned below.

- Header spec: noted. Amit, can you share the header tag mapping with Ben and our runtime folks before Wed? (owner: Amit)
- KMS/PII: security checklist will be sent with the tracing spec. Marissa, please include KMS integration notes and required artifacts for SOC2 review. (owner: Marissa)
- Cost delta: Ben — can you look at overhead ranges for per-request tracing vs. sampling and share a ballpark by Tue? (owner: Ben)

Internal action items
- Ben: produce a short note (1–2 slides) on expected latency/cost overhead for full tracing vs sampling + caching strategies. Due Tue 5/25 EOD.
- Marissa: draft 6-week POC scope and acceptance criteria (metrics, success thresholds) and link to DocuSign procurement template. Due Mon 5/24.
- Soojin: share dashboard mock and tracing hook spec by Tue 5/25 morning.

Tech dive suggestions
- Agenda: 1) tracing hooks & span attributes, 2) dashboard walkthrough, 3) evals & reference prompt coverage, 4) rollout/rollback triggers and canary thresholds, 5) compliance & KMS questions.
- Suggested attendees: your infra lead, security, product; our runtime lead, CS, and solutions engineer.

I’ll send a calendar invite for Wed 5/26 1:00–2:00pm PT unless you prefer Thu.

—
Soojin

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Chris Dalton <chris@finlogic.co>, Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Amit Shah <amit.shah@finlogic.co>
Date: Sun, 23 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery: observability + evals — reference prompts, tracing hooks, SLO checklist

Thanks all — happy to own the POC scope and run the pilot. Quick commitments from CS side:

- We’ll instrument an eval pipeline that runs nightly against the seed reference prompts and surfaces an email digest for any prompt-level regressions > 10% failure change vs baseline.
- Provide an initial dashboard pack (Overview, Route drilldowns, Regression alerts, Cost summary) for the tech dive.
- Draft KMS integration checklist and list of artifacts for your security team (FinLogic) to review.

I'll attach the eval_checklist.pdf for your review and link the DocuSign procurement stub in the Drive.

Proposed POC acceptance criteria (summary)
- Regression detection: detect and notify on >10% relative drop for any monitored route within 48 hours.
- Cost transparency: per-route cost report published daily; variance vs estimate < 15% during POC.
- Rollout safety: automated canary with 1% traffic ramp, rollback if P50 latency increases > 25% or regression alerts fire.

If that aligns, we’ll confirm the DocuSign and calendar invites today.

—
Marissa Cole
Customer Success, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
